cli.about: Media organizer: scan sources into a plan, apply the plan, undo
cli.long:
Media organizer. Files from the config's sources are sorted into targets (in list order; the AI is one more condition), land in a plan and are processed only after that.

Workflow: `gallery scan -c gallery.toml -o plan.json`, review the summary and the plan, `gallery apply plan.json`; `gallery undo plan.report.json` undoes a run.

Working through a server: `scan --server` builds a plan with server paths; the plan is copied to the server, `gallery apply` runs there, and the report comes back via Syncthing next to the plan.

Sources are not changed in place: they go to the trash only after all outputs of their target are written and verified. If an output lies in the source's own folder and does not change the content, the source is not copied but renamed in place (and does not go to the trash); a file that already has the right name is left out of the plan ("unchanged"). GALLERY_TRASH=folder uses a .gallery-trash folder instead of the system trash. The AI key is taken from ANTHROPIC_API_KEY or CLAUDE_API_KEY.
cli.lang: Message language: en, ru, uk, de, fr, es, pt-BR, it, pl, ro, zh-CN
cli.check.long: Shows the external tools (ffmpeg, ffprobe, exiftool, avifenc, magick, optipng), their versions and ffmpeg's capabilities. Exit code 1 if a required tool or capability is missing. Tools are looked up in GALLERY_TOOLS_DIR, then in PATH. With --config the config file is loaded and validated first (a one-line notice if it still uses the old before_ai / ai / after_ai shape); an invalid config is an error.
cli.scan.about: Scan the sources and write a plan
cli.scan.long: Scans the sources, reads EXIF, sorts files into targets and writes the plan. Prints a summary: files per target, the review list, unmatched files, warnings, AI cost. Nothing but the plan file is changed. Unsure AI answers go to review unless --accept-low is given.
cli.scan.estimate: Only estimate the AI cost (how many files would be sent, how many are cached), no calls and no plan
cli.scan.server: Plan with server paths (server_path of the sources)
cli.scan.no_ai: Skip the AI: no `ai` condition holds, files go on to the later targets
cli.apply.long: Applies a plan. Refuses to run if a tool lacks a needed capability. Changed or missing sources are skipped. The report is written next to the plan as <plan>.report.json. Exit code 2 if any file failed.
cli.apply.pilot: Pilot: apply only N files per target, write the rest to a separate plan
cli.apply.allow_anomalies: Place results that differ from the source (date, mtime, GPS, size, duration)
cli.apply.pause_sync: Pause the local Syncthing folders the plan touches and do not resume them
cli.sync.about: Syncthing folders paused by this program
cli.sync.long: Works only with a local Syncthing (address and key come from its config.xml). `status` shows what is paused; `resume` resumes only those folders and clears the pause record.
cli.sync.status.about: What is paused and whether Syncthing answers
cli.sync.resume.about: Resume the folders this program paused
cli.explain.about: Explain why a file gets the treatment it gets
cli.explain.long: Shows what a scan does with each file: which source it is in, which target filters take it and why not (match, exclude, `!`), what the manual decision or the AI decided, which content and name steps fired, where the file will end up, and a one-line verdict with a hint. Changes nothing and never calls the AI: a cached answer is used if there is one.
cli.unmatched.about: Triage "unmatched": which files, and why no target takes them
cli.unmatched.long: Groups the plan's unmatched files by source, folder and extension and prints for each group the file count, size and reason (as `explain` does). Without --plan the plan is built on the fly without AI, but with the metadata and groups a scan reads, so conditions on dates, places, duplicates and so on hold. Changes nothing.
cli.unmatched.plan: A finished plan (JSON); without it a new one is built without AI
cli.unmatched.overrides: Manual decisions file for the on-the-fly plan
cli.pending.about: How many files are pending (for scripts and cron)
cli.pending.long: Quietly counts how many files a scan would put into targets and how many wait for an AI answer (not in the cache). The AI is not called and nothing changes except a small index in the user's cache: on a repeated call EXIF is read only for new and changed files. The first line is `pending: N`; --json prints everything as one object.
cli.install_desktop.about: Write the app's .desktop file (application menu) for gallery-gui
cli.install_desktop.long: Writes ~/.local/share/applications/gallery.desktop (Exec points to gallery-gui next to this program, or to --exe) and an icon to ~/.local/share/icons. Never runs on its own.
cli.install_desktop.exe: Path to gallery-gui (default: next to this executable)
cli.examples.about: AI examples: your corrections of its answers
cli.examples.long: When you change what the AI decided (or resolve a doubtful answer), the correction is remembered as text (no images) and shown to the AI as an example in later requests for the same source; how many examples go into a request is set by `[ai] examples` (default 20, 0 turns it off). `list` shows them, `clear` deletes them. Examples affect only new AI requests: answers already in the cache stay valid.
cli.examples.list.about: Show the corrections the AI sees
cli.examples.clear.about: Delete corrections (all or of one source)
cli.presets.long: Prints the built-in name and content presets with their key parameters. They can be used in the config by name without a definition; a user preset with the same name is an error.
cli.undo.about: Undo a run from its report
cli.undo.long: Restores the sources from the trash and deletes the outputs the run created. Outputs changed after the run stay. A report can be undone once.
